direct_answer: A separate climate transition plan (as detailed in ESRS) does not exist: Neste states it "does not have a separate climate transition plan as detailed in the ESRS" and will "evaluate the development of specific climate transition plan" (e.g., to align with the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive) [Source 1]. Because no separate ESRS-style transition plan exists, 1.5°C alignment of a transition plan cannot be confirmed from the provided passages; while Neste uses an IEA "Net Zero World 2050" scenario that is "in line with the 1.5 ℃ pathways" in its scenario analysis, this is not presented as a disclosed 1.5°C-aligned transition plan [Source 5].
compliance_rationale: ESRS E1-1 expects disclosure of whether a transition plan exists and, if it exists, how targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C. Neste explicitly discloses that it does not have a separate ESRS-style climate transition plan and only indicates it will evaluate developing one [Source 1]. The passages provided do not include the required explanation that a transition plan’s GHG targets are compatible with 1.5°C; they only evidence use of a 1.5°C-aligned scenario in scenario analysis [Source 5].
disclosure_gaps: No disclosed ESRS E1-1 transition plan document/structure (company states none exists) [Source 1].

No explicit statement that a transition plan is 1.5°C aligned, nor explanation of compatibility of GHG targets with 1.5°C in the context of a transition plan (not evidenced in provided passages) [Source 1].

No details (in provided passages) on decarbonisation levers/key actions, investments and funding, locked-in emissions assessment, and progress against a transition plan as required by ESRS E1-1 (beyond general statements) [Source 1].

No substantiation (in provided passages) under ESRS E1-4 that GHG targets are science-based/1.5°C compatible, including methodology/scenarios used to set targets (only scenario analysis is described, not target-setting) [Source 5].
key_findings: Neste states it does not have a separate climate transition plan as detailed in ESRS; it relies on targets, actions, resource plans and an internal carbon price to support climate change mitigation transition [Source 1].
Neste will evaluate developing a specific climate transition plan (e.g., aligned with the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive) [Source 1].
Neste is excluded from EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks because it derives revenue from refining fossil fuels [Source 1].

Neste’s scenario analysis includes an IEA-based "Net Zero World 2050" scenario that is in line with 1.5°C pathways, but this is described as scenario analysis rather than a 1.5°C-aligned transition plan [Source 5].
